articles.body:
The Skyrim guild known as The Companions have quests reminiscent of the Fighter's Guild quests from past Elder Scrolls games, but are less generically named. Plus, this band of warriors also has a trick up its sleeve.

The Companions is by far the easiest guild to join, and can be done within the first few hours of your playthrough. To start The Companions story, simply go to Jorrvaskr, the large hall in the northeast of Whiterun.

Speak to Kodlak Whitemane inside to start the Take Up Arms quest that introduces you to the guild's key members, Vilkas, Aela, and Farkas. You'll officially join the guild during this quest, though it's more busywork than anything warrior-like. You'll get more of that in The Companions' second quest, Proving Honor .

There are 18 Companions quests , six of which are main missions (starting with Take Up Arms and finishing with Glory of the Dead) and the rest are actually endlessly repeatable radiant quests, making it a great faction to grind for XP:

articles.title: Dragonslayer Walkthrough - The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Following immediately after finding the ancient heroes in Sovngarde, Dragonslayer is the final main quest of Skyrim, concluding the dragon story arc. This
articles.body:
Following immediately after finding the ancient heroes in Sovngarde , Dragonslayer is the final main quest of Skyrim , concluding the dragon story arc. This quest centers entirely around a boss fight against Alduin, the World-Eater. Below, you'll find our tips and tricks for killing Alduin.

Help the heroes of Sovngarde dispel Alduin's mist

Resolution is nigh! Walk outside of the hall with the heroes and cross the bridge. Once on the other side of the bridge, you will be told to clear the mist together. Use your Clear Skies Shout three times to dissipate the mist and call Alduin down, starting the boss fight.

The only thing you absolutely have to try your best to do is just keep Alduin on the ground and stun him as much as possible, so use Dragonrend to force him down. Once on the ground, your goal is simple: deal as much damage as you can before he takes off, just like every other dragon. However, this time, you'll also have the help of the three Nord heroes.

Aside from using Dragonrend, you'll want to let the Nord heroes take Alduin's attention before attacking. Then, attack him from the sides if you're using melee weapons to avoid his fire breath and tail swipes, or attack him from a distance with bows/magic if you're a ranged character. You should also use the Marked for Death shout to reduce Alduin's armor resistance and drain health for 60 seconds.

Fire resistance (either from potions or enchantments) will be very helpful if you're taking lots of damage on harder difficulties, but generally speaking, Alduin is surprisingly easy to kill for the so-called 'World-Eater' come to end the world.

Once Alduin is dead, talk to Tsun and he will teach you a new Shout , Call of Valor, which allows you to summon the ancient heroes. He will then send you on your merry way back to the living world.

You should end up at the Throat of the World with many dragons surrounding you. If you didn't kill Paarthurnax, he will talk to you and tell you that now that all the dragons no longer have a leader, he will do his best to persuade them to follow the ways of the voice and fly away.

Congratulations after you have completed this quest you will have completed the main storyline of Skyrim.

While you've just completed the main story, you are never done with Skyrim!

Guilds and Factions : Join one (or all) of the factions and complete their stories. The College of Winterhold - Become a master mage. The Companions - Become a warrior. The Dark Brotherhood - Become an assassin. Thieves Guild - Become a master thief.

Dawnguard DLC : Complete the first expansion, focused on vampires and vampire-hunters.

Dragonborn DLC : Complete the second expansion to learn more about the Dragonborns.

Mutations : Become a vampire or werewolf.

Secrets : Find everything hiding in Skyrim.

articles.title: How Percy Jackson and the Olympians Is Finally Getting Adaptation Right
articles.summary: Percy Jackson and the Olympians is out on Disney+ now, and IGN has an interview with the cast and crew breaking down how they're getting the adaptation right this time.
articles.body:
For many fans of Rick Riordan’s Percy Jackson & the Olympians book series, the feature film adaptations from the early 2010s were disappointing. The characters were teenaged, the hero’s journey truncated, and it ultimately felt like an icky cash grab. However, the new Disney+ series seems to be the adaptation fans have been longing for. As our reviewer points out, the first four episodes are completely faithful to the books – almost to a fault. Yet, all the choices this adaptation has made, such as making it a TV series versus a film franchise; the bigger budget platform and technology of Disney+; and Riordan’s hand-picked actors to play Percy, Annabeth, and Grover characters all point to this series hitting all the marks it failed to the first time around.

While a Disney imprint published the Percy Jackson books since its beginning, 20th Century Studios acquired the film rights in 2004 and thus produced the fan-maligned 2010 and 2013 films. Riordan has shared his restricted experience as a consultant on those movies on his blog, along with his detailed notes on the various ways those scripts disregard the books’ spirit. When Disney bought the larger 21st Century Fox conglomerate in 2019, Rick likened those film rights reverting to the Mouse House to it “coming home” on his blog.

Executive Producers Dan Shotz and Jon Steinberg, who were also interested in adapting the books for Disney were also following the saga of the film rights, “It had gotten complicated. We then got a phone call a year-and-a-half later [after the Disney-Fox merger] saying, ‘Rick Riordan wants to think about maybe making this show again. Are you interested?’”

Riordan, along with his wife Becky, and Shotz and Steinberg collaborated throughout the pandemic to bring his beloved characters to life. “We started this four years ago, right at the beginning of COVID. We got to be in this little bubble, the four of us, and just dive into the story and really understand what it means to the fan base, what it means to his family. This is like a third child for them,” Shotz notes.

The goal of any adaptation is to capture the spirit of the source material while helping it adjust to its current time and medium, but that’s a lot easier said than done. The Riordans’ role as executive producers is to “sort of be the police of that spirit to make sure that it's authentic,” Becky comments. “It's not about how it looks or what the characters look like or any of that, but how it feels, how it resonates with fans of the books.”

Rick describes the DNA of his books as a “mix of adventure, a little bit of snark, a good amount of humor, and some heart with the characters really learning what it is to be friends and what it means to be a hero and step up and do hard things.”

However, the spirit of the books couldn’t truly be captured without the trio at the center: Percy Jackson (Walker Scobell), Annabeth Chase (Leah Sava Jeffries), and Grover Underwood (Aryan Simhadri). It helps that these young actors have been fans of the books since they were kids themselves. When asked what they related to most about their characters, each listed something that gave some insight into how they approached playing them.

Percy’s sense of humor was most appealing to Scobell, and Jeffries sees a balance of “independence and vulnerability” in Annabeth that she connects to, but Simhadri shares a pretty funny anecdote about his connection to Grover, “I liked him so much when I read the book series. And mostly because he could talk to animals. I convinced myself if I tried hard enough, I could also hear what animals were thinking… and I ended up getting attacked by a pigeon in the fourth grade.”

As mentioned before, the Riordans had no expectation of what the characters should look like, regardless of how they were depicted in the books, and Steinberg and Shotz also felt the same. When asked what characteristics they were looking for in terms of casting the trio, Steinberg chalks it up to Scobell, Jeffries, and Simhadri having the “it” factor. “I tried to be really careful before we started to not come to the process with a preconceived idea of what anybody's target was going to be,” he starts. “I had these characters in my head. They existed on a script page. We just watched these kids and the choices they made, hoping that there were going to be kids who came in and just made it so apparent that they were the kid. There's no manual for how to make sure that happens. We just got very, very lucky that that happened three times with each one of those kids. They all made it impossible to choose anyone else.”

When trolls and self-proclaimed “purists” came out of the woodwork to complain about the casting choices, Riordan directly addressed those ugly comments on his blog. He praised all three of the leads for their performances and what they individually bring to the characters. He also rhetorically asks why his opinion as the creator of these characters is not enough for these supposed fans. As for the time in production with the leads, Rick said in our interview that, “Our primary goal as a production has been to make sure the kids feel supported and that they feel safe and they feel good about what they're doing. The secondary goal is to make a great TV show. So if I've told the kids anything over the last year or two years, it's been, ‘What can we do for you? How are you feeling? Do you need a break?’ But also just, ‘You guys are awesome. You're doing the right thing. Do what you do. We got your back.’ That's really all it is.”

Percy Jackson and the Olympians Episodes 1-4 Gallery

It’s fair to say that TV is the ideal format to adapt a sprawling book franchise, and for all parties involved, there was never any question that the Disney+ adaptation would be a series. Steinberg says that it would be too difficult to take this story and adapt it into a 90-minute runtime. “It just doesn't want that.” Rick even acknowledges the easy translation of his book to a series, “I write in an episodic way: we do this, this happens here, and then they go here and this happens. It neatly breaks out into distinct episodes.”

In that spirit, the show uses the book’s chapter titles to name the episodes. The first four episodes are, in order, “I Accidentally Vaporize My Pre-Algebra Teacher”, “I Become Supreme Lord of the Bathroom”, “We Visit the Garden Gnome Emporium”, and “I Plunge to My Death,” effectively covering the first thirteen chapters of Percy Jackson and the Lightning Thief. This gives audiences an idea of the season’s pacing, with the last nine chapters of the first book covered in the later four episodes. “With eight episodes, we have more time to tell the whole story of the first book [...] and even add some things and deepen our understanding of who the characters are,” Rick teases.

The Riordans also had fun toying with the TV format to bring new dimensions to characters and moments he wrote so many years ago, “It was absolutely fabulous,” Becky says. “TV lends itself more to multiple points of view,” Rick adds. “So we just kind of leaned into that. And while it is from Percy's point of view this season, you also get those snapshots of what's going on when Percy's not around.”

In the books, the readers can only get an impression of how those around Percy feel based on his interpretation. Now, in adapting to the television medium, we get a better perspective of the world that surrounds our protagonist rather than only seeing things through his lens.

Steinberg also touches on this idea. “As the show gets deeper into its story, you start to get a feel for which other characters you might want to just spend a minute with.” He particularly praises Simhadri’s performance as Grover as one that inspired a fun one-on-one scene between Grover and Ares (Adam Copeland) that wasn’t in the books. “You wouldn't have known that was going to exist until you watched Aryan breathe life into that character,” Steinberg continues. “And then, once he did, it was the most obvious thing in the world.”

Simhadri also describes that scene with Ares, whose entire plot was left out of the movie. “Adam Copeland killed it as Ares. He was so terrifying. I'm not acting there. I'm sitting in a cafe with him and it's this intense interrogation scene and none of that is fake. I am genuinely scared for my life.” Though Simhadri quickly clarifies, “He’s such a nice guy.”

Speaking of gods, Shotz mentions the advantages of adapting a completed series, “We could really look at where [Rick] was going with the story, which he didn't even have the benefit of twenty years ago. We got to take advantage of that. Even though we are keeping as true to The Lightning Thief as we can, we could also bring gods you might not see until later and hint at them or see them in season one. That was pretty exciting to have that whole well of material to work off of.”

Equipped with Disney’s production budget and ILM’s newest StageCraft LED Volume stage in Vancouver, the possibilities of how to portray the mythical domains of Hell and Olympus are limitless. Steinberg points out a more subtle use of the Volume that even fooled the professionals. “One of my favorite moments in the show was hearing that there were people in the post-production pipeline who saw the footage of the interior of The Met and didn't realize we didn't just get back from New York.”

“Being able to partner with them across the board for that, and our VFX, our creatures, and our design work, you can't get better than that,” Shotz adds. “All those guys are fathers with kids that were looking at them and being like, ‘Dad, deliver this. Mom, deliver this right.’ There was pressure on that front, but it was worth it.”

“ILM killed it,” gushes Simhadri. “They didn't leave anything up to the imagination unless they had to. All of the huge, big set pieces were really cool. We played Mario Kart on the Volume stage when we wrapped.” When asked who won, both Jeffries and Simhadri reply, “Me,” while Scobell smiles between them.

It’s been a long struggle for fans of the Percy Jackson books to see the live-action adaptation they deserve, but with the Riordans fully and passionately involved, much more time and space to tell this story, and the full force of Disney’s expansive visual effects behind them, it seems like everything is smooth sailing.

Some quotes have been condensed or edited for clarity.

articles.title: Percy Jackson and the Olympians Season 1 Review - IGN
articles.summary: A new addition to the pantheon of YA adaptations.
articles.body:
The following review contains spoilers for the entire first season of Percy Jackson and the Olympians.

Looking at the entirety of Percy Jackson and the Olympians’ first season, it’s easy to see the care that was put into its plotting and execution. There’s an obvious effort to keep this second attempt at a screen adaptation of Rick Riordan’s YA novels true to its source material – and, in the process, create a streaming series that could continue beyond Percy Jackson’s (Walker Scobell) initial adventure among the gods and monsters of Greek mythology. It’s an energy that runs through every aspect of season 1, even when the execution is lacking. And most of the time it isn’t.

Much of the love can be seen in the production value. For a Disney+ project, Percy Jackson and the Olympians often punches above its weight class, both visually and sonically. The quality may vary from episode to episode, but overall it’s a really good looking piece of television with an incredible score from Bear McCreary ( The Walking Dead , God of War Ragnarök ), which is refreshing in an era when TV production is so rampant and budgets are spread so thin that show’s often can’t look or sound good.

Percy Jackson Season 1: Episodes 1-8 Gallery

Smart directing can improve the appearance of CGI, and that’s often the case here. Such visual effects are used strategically; Grover’s (Aryan Simhadri) satyr legs represent their only week-in, week-out requirement. The more challenging, immersive environments like Hades and Olympus are unevenly rendered on Disney’s Volume stage, but elements like the Minotaur, Medusa, and Waterworld mix CGI and practical effects cleanly. This approach elevates Percy Jackson in a way other shows could learn from.

Riordan’s novels are steeped in family and friendship, and without the right casting, all of that could’ve been lost. Thankfully, almost every member of the cast is pitch-perfect for their role. From the main three of Percy, Grover, and Annabeth (Leah Jeffries) all the way down to the fan-favorite (or at least my favorite) Gabe (Timm Sharp), each character feels lifted directly from the pages of Percy Jackson and the Lightning Thief. They’re embodied in a way that outweighs any of the shortcomings in the younger cast members’ performances or the dialogue.

Writing is the series’ Achilles heel. The dialogue is often overly expositional, stilted, and unnatural, leading to unconvincing line readings. It’s a problem that plagues plot-heavy projects (and specifically literary adaptations) that have a lot of ground to cover and limited time to cover it, and Percy Jackson and the Olympians is no exception. Even with the benefit of a longer runtime, trying to fit all of a book’s finer details into a season of TV can leave things feeling overstuffed. That’s felt in Percy Jackson’s pacing as well, with episodes like “ I Become Supreme Lord of the Bathroom ” and “ We Take a Zebra to Vegas ” squeezing longer Lightning Thief passages into a single episode.

Percy Jackson and the Olympians is strongest when it focuses on the familial and fraternal elements of its story, and lets its young actors play young. There are some truly emotionally adept moments throughout the first season that highlight the love between mothers and sons, and discuss parenting in a way that’s both simple enough for young viewers to grasp and deep enough to satisfy parents and other adult viewers. It’s fun for the whole family! I’m excited for the series to potentially continue and tell more stories in this mythical world. It just needs to do so before Scobell, Simhadri, and Jeffries age out of their characters.

articles.title: Percy Jackson Author Rick Riordan Reveals He Has Dozens of Unfinished Novels
articles.summary: The novelist behind the blockbuster series of young adult books breaks down what he can't wait for fans to see in the new episodes on Disney+.
articles.body:
Rick Riordan, the author of the wildly popular Percy Jackson series of young adult novels , loves to write. To date, he’s published more than 50 fantasy and adventure books covering modern-day spins on Greek, Roman, and Egyptian mythology. Riordan, who at one time was a middle school English teacher, says that beyond all of his published works, he’s left as many or (potentially) more stories on the cutting room floor, dating back to his time as a student.

I spoke with Riordan ahead of the Season 2 premiere of the Disney+ adaptation of his Percy Jackson series of novels about the particular challenges of bringing a now-beloved franchise to life.

“The hardest part of writing a book is finishing it, and I am not saying that to be snide or anything,” Riordan says. “When I was in sixth grade, I knew I wanted to be a writer, but I couldn't make myself finish even a short story. I would get halfway through and say, 'Oh, this is too hard. I'll try another one, and that'll be easier.' I have dozens of unfinished stories [and] novels from when I was that age. The hardest thing is to say, 'I know I don't like this right now' – what I'm in the middle of writing – 'but I'm going to finish it anyway and then I'll go back and read it and see how it is.' That's the difference between getting it done and not getting it done.”

Riordan says when he got older and began writing the Percy Jackson novels, there was one character in particular that he put more than a little bit of himself into. “A writer once said that you can't write a character who is not in some part you, that doesn't have at least a sliver of your personality. I think overall, I feel most drawn to [Camp Half-Blood Activities Director] Chiron, the centaur. We're both teachers and it is our job not to tell kids what they need to think or what to do, but to help them figure that out for themselves, to coach them into becoming their own heroes. Teaching, I think at its best, is exactly that.”

Season 2 of Percy Jackson and the Olympians, adapted from Riordan’s novel The Sea of Monsters, just dropped its first two episodes on Disney+. Riordan says there’s one fan-favorite scene in particular he can’t wait for the audience to see.

“I think the scene with the sirens is very important,” Riordan says. “That's a pivotal scene in the relationship between Annabeth and Percy. It’s something that fans love. It's become a touchstone for them. They're looking for that scene, and I know a lot of eyes are going to be on it, so we paid a lot of attention to it to make sure we're doing it right [in a way] that it is both faithful to what's in the book but also a little bit surprising.”

Percy Jackson: 20th Century Film vs Disney+ Series

As the new season of the TV show rolls out, Riordan is eager for fans to watch and understand just how much work into crafting the blockbuster adaptation.

“I think the entire process would be eye-opening [to fans],” Riordan says. “I don't think that it's possible to appreciate how much work is involved until you've actually walked on the set. In fact, I had this experience just a couple of weeks ago. My literary agents for Percy Jackson came to visit us on the set in Vancouver, and they've been with Percy Jackson for 20 years. They have been in every conversation. They know this stuff intimately, and I've been keeping them updated. Nevertheless, until they were on set and walking through the studio, they turned to me and said, ‘Now I get it. I had no idea.’ You have to be there to understand it.”

Percy Jackson and the Olympians, Season 2: Episodes 1 and 2 are streaming now on Disney+. New episodes premiere each Wednesday. Read our review of the first two episodes here. And for more on Percy Jackson, check out what to expect form the series' new Fortnite island .

Michael Peyton is the Senior Editorial Director of Events & Entertainment at IGN, leading entertainment content and coverage of tentpole events including IGN Live, San Diego Comic Con, gamescom, and IGN Fan Fest. He's spent 20 years working in the games and entertainment industry, and his adventures have taken him everywhere from the Oscars to Japan to Buenos Aires, Argentina. Follow him on Bluesky @MichaelPeyton

articles.title: Contraptions and Mechanisms Walkthrough - Enshrouded Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Contraptions and Mechanisms is a side quest in Enshrouded that opens up a whole new way to play: creating deadly gauntlets to challenge yourself and your
articles.body:
Contraptions and Mechanisms is a side quest in Enshrouded that opens up a whole new way to play: creating deadly gauntlets to challenge yourself and your friends. By the end of this quest, you’ll have a Sparkworks Workbench, where you can create levers, buttons, and all manner of deadly traps. This side quest walkthrough will show you how to complete the quest so you can get to building your most dastardly dungeon idea.

How to Start Contraptions and Mechanisms

You can start Contraptions and Mechanisms after getting the Carpenter settled into your camp. Once he’s sheltered and set up, ask him about “Our Own Contraptions” to get started.

How to Complete Contraptions and Mechanisms

To complete Contraptions and Mechanisms, you need to make your way through a Night Sanctum near the Revelwood Ancient Spire. Wait for nighttime and glide southeast from the spire to find the door on the other side of a tall, grassy cliff. The image above is captured in the daytime so you know what you’re looking for, but remember that you can only open the sanctum at night.

Once inside, take a look to your right to read a Lore entry about a scholar who spent some time here before.

For the first trap, wait for the upper spike bar to approach and then run into the hallway. Hop over the lower bar and you should still have plenty of time to make it to the other side.

Hop down in the next chamber and continue to trap number two: a narrow walkway with two electrical traps. Time your steps to go between the blasts to reach the other end. Stop at the end of the walkway to line yourself up for the last trap.

The last hallway has three spinning spike columns moving on rails through the room. When the center one reaches your side, follow after it until just before you reach the opposite end. Then, weave around it to reach the final room.

With that, you’ve navigated all the traps. Drop down and continue through the halls to collect the Sparkworks Tool from the gold chest at the end.

Fast travel back to your settlement and speak to the Carpenter to take a look at the recipe for the Sparkworks Workbench. That’s the production place you’ll actually use to craft your contraptions. The tool is just for placing things. You’ll need:

Nails x2: Made from Metal Scraps by the Blacksmith.

Metal Sheets x4: Made from Metal Scraps at the Forge.

Archaic Essence x8: Collected from Shroud Lairs.

Copper Bars x2: Forged from Copper Ore at the Smelter.

Once you’ve build the Sparkworks Workbench, place it somewhere convenient for you to complete the quest. You’ll earn 100 XP and you’ll be well on your way to developing your very first dastardly dungeon.

articles.title: Dark Rites Walkthrough - Enshrouded Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Dark Rites is a main quest in Enshrouded that has you search Pikemead’s Reach for a hidden attic used for conducting profane rituals. It’s a
articles.body:
Dark Rites is a main quest in Enshrouded that has you search Pikemead’s Reach for a hidden attic used for conducting profane rituals. It’s a mysterious quest that’ll get you a new Assistant in your settlement. This walkthrough will show you how to start and end this quest with one trip to the capital city.

To start the Dark Rites quest, you must find a Lore page in Pikemead’s Reach titled “A Small Thank You.” You can find it in a ruined home near the east entrance to Pikemead’s Reach. It’s on the ground floor, and reading it also begins the Ramone’s Writing quest.

To complete Dark Rites, you must follow the clues to learn of the dark ritual that some of the survivors were attempting in Pikemead’s Reach. The first stop is in the Imperial Garden’s District, in a secret attic at the top of one of its larger buildings. To get there, u se the grapple point sticking out of one of the buildings on the west side of the district .

Head up the ladder you find there to reach a small perch on the roof. Then, glide across to the building to the north .

Walk all the way to the opposite side of this attic space and turn into the room on your right. In the far left corner of that room, you’ll find a bookshelf. Behind it, another, shabbier bookshelf that you can break down. Destroy it and read the Lore page on the ground titled “Ritual of Reunion” to continue to the next step of the quest.

That Lore page told of someone named Lady Leclair, who attempted this ritual in her home in Glennwood’s End. You can glide to that town from the Revelwood Ancient Spire . You’ll have to put your feet on the ground between two large mountains blocking your way, but the road you find there will take you all the way up to the center of town.

You’re looking for an isolated building on the west side of town , just outside the main walls. Hop over the walls and up the stairs to enter through the front door.

Once inside, read the Lore page on the table against the far wall to learn more about Lady Leclair’s ritual. Then, descend down the cobweb-covered chimney , to find her secret basement.

Inside the secret basement, you’ll find Lady Leclair’s skeleton on a table. Collect her soul and summon her in your settlement to complete this quest. Your Alchemist will now have a fancy new Assistant, and you’ll gain 300 XP for your trouble.

articles.title: Nice Day For Fishing Walkthrough - Enshrouded Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Nice Day For Fishing is a side quest in Enshrouded that serves as a tutorial for high-level fishing in Veilwater Basin. In it, you’ll acquire the
articles.body:
Nice Day For Fishing is a side quest in Enshrouded that serves as a tutorial for high-level fishing in Veilwater Basin. In it, you’ll acquire the necessary bait and capture an epic fish for use in some of the game’s best cooking recipes. This side quest walkthrough will show you the best place to get it all done.

To start Nice Day For Fishing, you must first resurrect the Fisher, Captain Melville Fontane. As soon as you summon him into your settlement, ask him about “Nice Day For Fishing” and he’ll start you on this quest.

The first step in Nice Day For Fishing is to capture some Frogs for use as bait. You’ll find them all over Veilwater Basin in tall grass near bodies of water. There’s usually at least two groups of them on Fishing Island, which is a short glide southwest from the Ancient Spire.

With the Frogs collected, head back to your settlement and speak to the Fisher again. He’ll offer the Excellent Fishing Rod recipe, which you can build now with the following resources:

Tropical Wood x1: Gathered from chopping down trees in Veilwater Basin.

Steel Bars x1: Made from Iron Ore at the Blast Furnace.

Gold Dust x1: Ground up from Gold Ore at the Mill.

Gold Coins x1: Found in loot throughout Embervale.

With your new fishing rod in hand, head back to Fisher’s Island and cast off the small pier to catch yourself a fish. These epic fish put up quite a fight, so you’ll need to watch your Fishing Endurance carefully. The trick is to never stop pulling away from the fish, even when it stops moving . Watch the indicator bar at the top, and whenever it shifts to the fish’s side, switch directions. If you’re having trouble, you can also pick up the Fisherman’s Resolve skill in the center section of the skill wheel.

It might take a few tries, but you will eventually pull up an epic-grade fish. Take it back to the Fisher and show it to him to complete the quest and earn 400 XP.

articles.title: The Best LEGO Lord of the Rings Sets for 2026
articles.summary: LEGO has been in a lull recently when it comes to Lord of the Rings sets, but a couple of huge (and pricy) sets point to a more fruitful future.
articles.body:
Back in 2023, LEGO released Lord of the Rings Rivendell – a 6,000-piece tribute to Peter Jackson's vision of Middle-Earth and the J.R.R. Tolkien-written books that inspired it. You can check it out on Amazon . I reviewed the set for IGN and interviewed the designer in a follow-up feature. It is one of the best, most detail-oriented builds of the past five years.

In 2024, LEGO released another massive Lord of the Rings set, this time of Barad-dûr , the massive tower in Mordor that's topped with the Eye of Sauron. Similar to Rivendell, it is laden with numerous, movie-accurate details. Then 2025 brought us The Shire , another rich, albeit smaller build. And now, in 2026, we have Minas-Tirith , the fabled White City and capital of Gondor.

Every Lord of the Rings Set Available Now

LEGO The Lord of the Rings: Balrog Book Nook

LEGO Icons The Lord of The Rings: Sauron's Helmet

LEGO The Lord of the Rings: Minas Tirith

Currently, there are very few Lord of the Rings sets on sale, but this wasn't always the case. LEGO and Lord of the Rings first partnered in June 2012, and between June 2012 and October 2014, LEGO released numerous sets that celebrated both the original Lord of the Rings film trilogy and the subsequent Hobbit trilogy . The last of these went out of print in July 2015; the only way to obtain them now would be to go on the expensive secondary market.

Here is a showcase of the major LEGO Lord of the Rings sets over the past decade plus: what was released and subsequently retired; what is currently on sale; and what we might expect to see in the future.

And that brings us to the present day. On sale now exclusively at the LEGO Store, Rivendell sets a bar for the level of delicate detail that can exist in a single set. It is beautiful, but it is fragile, with some elements hanging on by single connections. Other details, like the leaves on the trees and the patterning of the roofs, create a cumulative intricacy. And many more details are enclosed, meant to be cast in shadow by the exterior elements. This is a set that you admire with your eyes and not with your hands, and is one of our picks for the best LEGO sets for adults .

We built this at launch . The most recently released set on this list, the LEGO rendition of Barad-dûr is nearly three feet tall and covered with menacing, black spikes. The interior includes a dungeon, Saruman's throne room, and a armory for the orcs and goblins to gird themselves for battle. On top is the glowing Eye of Sauron, which is backlit with a red light brick.

The latest Lord of the Rings set depicts The Shire on the evening of Bilbo's 111th Birthday. Go through the circular door into Bilbo's hobbit hole, and you'll see all sorts of cool details – food on every available surface, a study with an inkpot and quill, and an open foyer that is instantly recognizable from the first film. The coolest bit is the fireplace; turn a crank, and the wax-sealed envelope 'burns away' to reveal the One True Ring. We built and photographed this set at the time of its launch.

LEGO's line of book nooks is designed to fit on your bookshelf, thereby breaking up the monotony of the actual books with scenery from classic literature. This set captures the climactic battle between Gandalf and the Balrog, deep in the Mines of Moria. It even comes with a small "You Shall Not Pass!" plaque on its front. We built and photographed this set , and its size and scope make it a worthy addition to the franchise

Only seen during the flashback scenes in the films, Sauron's Helmet is a terrifying embodiment of evil in Middle-Earth. It's best remembered for its slow-motion fall after Isildur, son the of the King, sliced off Sauron's fingers during the War of the Last Alliance. This model is mounted on a stand alongside a minifigure of Sauron himself. We reviewed and photographed this set for its launch, and we were impressed by its visual accuracy .

As of 2026, this is the largest Lord of the Rings set in LEGO history . It is 'hybrid-scale'; while the exterior is microscale to capture the breadth and height of the White City, the inside is a minifigure-scaled and features an imposing replica of the Citadel's throne room. Also included are 10 minifigures, including Gandalf the White, Faramir, Denethor, Peregrin Took, Aragorn, and Arwen. We built and reviewed this set for its launch, and we named it as one of the 10 best LEGO sets currently available .

This set captured the moment when Aragorn defended Frodo and the Hobbits from the Ringwraiths. It included the key details, such as the spiral stone staircase that led to the top of the watchpoint, as well as the black horses that the Ringwraiths rode as they searched the realm for the One True Ring. This was part of the first wave of LEGO Lord of the Rings sets in June 2012, along with the second entry on this list.

This Mines of Moria sequence is one of the coolest parts of the Lord of the Ring movies . The set based on it included a massive cave troll and several freestanding elements to represent Balin's Tomb. The LEGO designers rigged the tomb to fall apart at the press of a lever, and you could also recreate the scene where Pippin knocked the skeleton into the well (via a trap door), thereby alerting everyone to the Fellowship's presence.

A small but richly detailed build, the Orc Forge was a blacksmith forge with fanciful elements, with a chain lift and bucket to transport ore, and a chute that fed into a cauldron to melt the ore down. It also included an anvil and a light brick to make the fire glow.

Based on the climactic siege that concluded The Two Towers, this was a massive castle set. It had the Horn of Helm Hammerhand at the top of its tallest tower, and its signature, curved outer wall, including a breakaway portion so you could recreate the moment when the orcs breached the defenses.

A charming build of Bilbo's home, An Unexpected Gathering included Gandalf, Bilbo, and 4 of the 12 dwarves who imposed themselves on his hospitality. Green was the predominant color of the set's exterior, which gave it the fertile, bountiful atmosphere that we associate with the Shire.

Obviously, the Battle of Black Gate, which was the climax to the entire LOTR trilogy, was much grander than what could be accomplished with 656 LEGO pieces. This is the exact sort of build that would most benefit from a modern reimagining. Can you picture what the LEGO designers could do with 3000 or even 4000 pieces? Still, there was lots to appreciate about this set, especially the Mouth of Sauron Minifigure, the Great Eagle, and the angular severity of the Gate itself.

This model of Saruman's massive tower was two-and-a-half feet tall, and it was as imposing as the LEGO designers had hoped. But as intimidating as the exterior was, the interior was equally impressive and included a throne room (where Gandalf and Saruman had their wizard duel), a dungeon, a library, and an alchemy room. It also comes with a massive Ent and a Great Eagle, so that Gandalf can hitch a ride off the roof.

This was Bilbo's big moment, when he discovered the entrance to the Lonely Mountain on Durin's Day. And this set includes the secret door, Smaug's lair, the mountain of gold, and a number of play mechanisms the dwarves' battle with Smaug, when they try to submerge him in liquid gold. This set was part of the last wave of Lord of the Rings sets from 2012-2014. We wouldn't get another set in the series until January 2023.

In January 2023, LEGO released several LOTR-themed pairings as part of their collectible Blockheadz line. There were four different sets available for purchase, each for $20: Gandalf the Grey & Balrog , Aragorn & Arwen , and Frodo & Gollum . LEGO retired them at the end of 2024.

How Many LEGO Lord of the Rings Sets are There?

According to the official LEGO Store , there are six Lord of the Rings sets available for purchase as of November 2026. Based on the past three years, one can assume that more sets, on the scale of Rivenedell , Barad-dûr , and Mina Tirith, will be on their own way. But perhaps, the comparatively smaller Shire set , not to mention the Balrog Book Nook, means that we'll get some variety in piece count.

There are rumors of a LEGO Oliphaunt, a model of the massive beast that appeared during the Battle of the Pelennor Fields in Return of the King. Maybe it'll come with a Legolas minifigure, since he took one down by himself ("That still only counts as one!")? If true, expect to see this set on shelves by the beginning of next year.

And as for the next, massive LEGO Lord of the Rings set? It's most likely Helm's Deep.

Why? Because eagle-eyed fans have been scrutinizing the stickers. There's a map sticker in the LEGO Rivendell set (2023) that shows Barad-dûr and Minas Tirith. Then, LEGO Barad-dûr (2024) had a map sticker with Minas Tirith and Helm's Deep. And now, here we are in 2026, and we have Minas Tirith too. If these stickers foreshadow what's coming next, maybe we'll get Helm's Deep in Summer 2027? We'll have to wait and see.

Kevin Wong is a contributing freelancer for IGN, specializing in LEGO. He's also been published in Complex, Engadget, Gamespot, Kotaku, and more. Follow him on Twitter at @kevinjameswong .

articles.title: 'We Can't Afford Kathryn Hahn': VisionQuest Creator Explains Why Agatha Harkness Didn't Appear
articles.summary: VisionQuest creator Terry Matalas has explained why Agatha Harkness failed to appear on screen during the series — despite her presence being felt.
articles.body:
VisionQuest creator Terry Matalas has explained why Agatha Harkness failed to appear on screen during the series — despite her presence being felt.

Before its launch, VisionQuest was described as the concluding chapter of the WandaVision trilogy (which began with WandaVision, and continued with Agatha All Along as its sandwich filling) — so there was some expectation that the sorceress from both series might reappear. But, alas, she did not — and Matalas has now explained why.

Warning: Spoilers for VisionQuest follow...

The finale of VisionQuest sees the return of Joe Locke's Billy Maximoff from Agatha All Along, as he reunites with Tommy Maximoff and his synthezoid sort-of father Vision. This picks up directly from WandaVision's final scene, where Billy sets off to go find his brother aided by a ghostly Harkness, who has now left her physical body behind.

While Agatha does not appear on screen in VisionQuest, Billy still talks briefly with her. Tommy even realizes that Billy is doing so, and makes a comment about his brother having an invisible friend — as Harkness does not appear to him (or the audience).

While it would have been great to see her physically (or spectrally) again, the dialogue is still a neat way of acknowledging her presence and confirming she's still helping Billy. But why not have Kathryn Hahn back for a cameo?

"We can't afford Kathryn Hahn!" Matalas told ScreenRant , acknowledging Hahn's absence. "First of all, the second you bring Kathryn Hahn into a scene, it's a Kathryn Hahn scene. It's really about Agatha, and in that moment of the reunion, it needed to be about Billy. [It] needed to be about Tommy.

"So you can't detract from the story you're trying to tell just because it would be neat to see Agatha," Matalas concluded, "and so that's really the core of it... It's got to be the story of these three characters: Vision, Tommy, and Billy."

VisionQuest then concluded with a shocking tease of Wanda Maximoff's return — just in time for next month's Avengers: Doomsday. Where will see the Maximoff family again, and could Agatha still return in future? Perhaps next month will provide the answers.

articles.title: Judge Denies Motion to Dismiss RAM Price Fixing Lawsuit
articles.summary: Even if you've been under a rock all year, it's hard to ignore the massive RAM crisis that's been going on since late 2025. And, while prices likely won't improve, it does seem like there's a small possibility that the three major RAM manufacturers might face some accountability.
articles.body:
Even if you've been under a rock all year, it's hard to ignore the massive RAM crisis that's been going on since late 2025. And while prices likely won't improve, it does seem like there's a small possibility that the three major RAM manufacturers might face some accountability.

A class action lawsuit accusing Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung of colluding to fix the price of RAM while simultaneously scaling back production was filed back in June. This kind of case will likely take years to go through the system. But the RAM companies filed a motion to dismiss the lawsuit, arguing that each company made "rational choices consistent with their own independent self interest" and that the case was just a "rerun" of a similar case from 2022. But on Friday, Judge Noël Wise denied the motion .

Wise's order references the previous case, which was dismissed, saying, "During the hearing, Defendants quoted the late Honorable Judge Posner who famously wrote, '[c]ompetitors in concentrated markets watch each other like hawks.'" But then added, "But Plaintiffs’ allegations go beyond hawks watching each other; their contentions are more akin to hawks flying in formation – an activity that hawks ordinarily do not do."

Now, before you go and celebrate that RAM prices are going to come crashing down, this order simply means that the case will move forward – the fight isn't over yet. This class action lawsuit will probably be moving through the courts for a couple years before any final decision is made.

While the previous 2022 class action was dismissed, the three companies named in this lawsuit do have a history of working together to manipulate the RAM market. All the way back in 2002, the U.S. Department of Justice investigated a "criminal cartel" made up of Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron in order to fix prices. That investigation ended in jail time for a Samsung executive, along with a $300 million fine for Samsung and a $185 million fine for SK Hynix.

If anything, though, the RAM market is worse for consumers than either of the two times that the three RAM companies have been accused of price fixing. According to the order, the last class action came after memory prices spiked by 165% in 2018. But compared to 2026, that's nothing. The order says, "In sum, Plaintiffs allege a 697% price increase for conventional DRAM over an eighteen-month period." Looking at RAM kits on Amazon, it's hard to deny that number.

Only time will tell how this lawsuit will play out, but no matter what happens, it doesn't seem like RAM prices are going to improve any time soon. Samsung told investors during its latest earnings call that "AI-driven demand [is] likely to further tighten supply shortages" next year. That was after all three memory manufacturers reported selling through their 2027 manufacturing capacity all the way back in August 2026 . It's no wonder that Xbox Project Helix is rumored to hit $1,800 .

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

One of the best ultra-portable laptops drops to its lowest price ever for Black Friday. For such a lightweight laptop built with premium materials, an OLED display and current generation components, all in an ultra-light sub 3 pound platform, the asking price of $650 is a steal. Let's also not forget just how expensive DDR5 memory is nowadays, and the $650 laptop is generously equipped with 16GB of it.

articles.title: Austin Creed Goes Viral After Pulling Off Explosive Real-Life Shoryuken in AEW Full Gear Match
articles.summary: Pro wrestler Austin Creed went viral over the weekend for pulling off an iconic fighting game move in real life, hitting his opponent with an explosive Shoryuken in a viral moment that took social media by storm.
articles.body:
Pro wrestler Austin Creed went viral over the weekend for pulling off an iconic fighting game move in real life, hitting his opponent with an explosive Shoryuken in a viral moment that took social media by storm.

Creed, alongside Kofi Kingston and Swerve Strickland, put on a stunning performance at AEW’s Full Gear event on Saturday, November 14. The trio took on Brody King, Hangman Page, and the masked Bandido for a 3v3 brawl that saw a number of props and weapons used in the fight, which are allowed by Texas Death Match rules.

One of these props was a Nintendo Power Glove, an old-school accessory for the Nintendo Entertainment System that was first released in 1989. Of course, being a pro wrestling match, this particular Power Glove had special powers that allowed its wearer to pull off some especially brutal moves.

Wake up ➡️⬇️↘️+👊🏾 — Austin Creed (@AustinCreedWins) November 15, 2026

During his turn with King, Creed pulled the Power Glove out of a bag and slipped it on — but he took a tad too long, getting whacked in the head and sent to his knees. King smacked him a second time, seemingly outdoing his rival before Creed suddenly stood and hit him with a Shoryuken, his fist exploding in sparks and sending King flying backwards.

The moment went viral within wrestling circles and the fighting game community. Players wasted no time joking about Creed’s “wakeup DP” and “reversal,” with legendary pro player Justin Wong comparing the move to Daigo Umehara’s famed “Umeshoryus.”

To explain these terms to non-fighting gamers, a ‘DP’ refers to a Dragon Punch, which is a category of uppercut-style special move. ‘Wakeup’ is the moment that a player’s character recovers after being knocked down, while a ‘reversal’ refers to a player successfully executing a move and striking the opposing character as soon as possible after being hit. In essence, Creed hit King with a reversal DP on wakeup — a move that King probably should have seen coming.

“Lmao he just stayed still without blocking on his wakeup, deserved to get hit by reversal DP,” prominent fighting game YouTuber Rooflemonger joked .

“This is the coldest thing I've seen in the ring in over two decades,” game artist CartelDel remarked .

“Totally invincible on frames 1-8,” another teased .

Creed is one of several pro wrestlers who have referenced fighting games in the ring; Kenny Omega famously uses moves like Street Fighter 5 ’s V-Trigger against his opponents, and even contributed to Alex’s moveset for Street Fighter 6. Cody Rhodes, who famously portrayed Guile in the 2026 Street Fighter movie , also showed up to WWE Summer Slam in full Guile attire — including the character’s iconic flat-top hairstyle.

IGN knows this thanks to filmmaker Robert Eggers , who directed Pattinson in The Lighthouse and just so happened to be at IGN’s Los Angeles studio today to do an interview about his next movie, Werwulf .

So what did Pattinson think of Werwulf? “Oh, he loved it, of course,” Eggers responded with a grin.

articles.summary: Rockstar has revealed a new batch of GTA 6 screenshots – and even a Weather Channel forecast – showcasing Leonida's dynamic weather.
articles.body:
Rockstar has revealed a new batch of GTA 6 screenshots – and even a Weather Channel forecast – showcasing Leonida's dynamic weather.

The 13-year wait for a proper return to Vice City is almost over, but with just days to go until launch, no one had any idea what to expect from the week. Would more details leak? Would Rockstar reveal more gameplay details? Would we get more gameplay footage? Either way, it's probably safe to say no one was expecting to check the forecast to find out the latest on GTA 6.

The Weather Channel struck when it published a series of screenshots showing Vice City covered in everything from torrential downpours to ocean fog. We even get a true-to-life breakdown of what we're seeing here, giving would-be Leonida citizens a chance to prep before the storm hits.

Heavy rain is kicking up a lot of moisture making visibility poor in many places in the Keys, luckily the local authorities have installed reflectors in some of the roads to help driving (better get your headlights fixed at Coastal Auto Care) — The Weather Channel (@weatherchannel) November 16, 2026

Heavy rain is kicking up a lot of moisture making visibility poor in many places in the Keys, luckily the local authorities have installed reflectors in some of the roads to help driving (better get your headlights fixed at Coastal Auto Care)

"Grand Theft Auto VI takes place in Leonida – a fictional world inspired by modern-day Florida, a landscape with one of the most unpredictable weather systems in the US," Rockstar VP of art: light and rendering Owen Shepherd said. "To match the fidelity of all aspects of what is the deepest, most immersive take on the Grand Theft Auto series yet, we had to completely reimagine our in-game weather systems to feel more localized, persistent, and above all dynamic. Weather can range with everything from clear blue skies to towering vertiginous cumulonimbus clouds, grounding players in a world through weather we hope Florida locals – and new visitors to Leonida – can appreciate."

Rockstar confirmed it had developed an "advanced" weather system when speaking to Game Informer in September. Another update that arrived shortly afterward revealed that Vice City could, in fact, be hit by simulated tropical storms and hurricanes. At the time, these were said to bring "heavy clouds, strong winds, dense atmospherics, and a lot of rain." That means more than simple visual changes as Leonida is overrun by Mother Nature.

These early details promised something a little more intense than the occasional shower, and now, we have our first look at what that might actually look like. While there's a lot of variety here, there's no reason to believe these six screenshots represent everything the skies of Leonida have to offer.

GTA 6 finally launches for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19, 2026. It's a long time coming, with only a little bit more waiting to go. Luckily, we've got plenty to keep you busy. For a better look at the Grand Theft Auto series' history of Easter Eggs, click here . You can also click here if you'd like to take a peek into how Rockstar pulls from real life to make its games feel realistic , and if you're interested in how the top content creators are prepping for launch, click here . Oh, and if you need an excuse to stay home this Thursday, Xbox (kind of) has you covered .

articles.title: How to Get and Complete All Ruins of Lordaeron Quests - WoW Forever Guide - IGN
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever features a variety of dungeons for players to explore for unique bosses, quest objectives, supplemental EXP, and some of the best
articles.body:
World of Warcraft: Forever features a variety of dungeons for players to explore for unique bosses, quest objectives, supplemental EXP, and some of the best gear for certain level brackets, especially early on. One such dungeon that makes its grand debut in WoW: Forever is the Ruins of Lordaeron, an ominous locale adjacent to the Horde's Undercity hub.

To take advantage of the full potential of this dungeon, you'll want to make sure to obtain and fulfill all the quests applicable to Ruins of Lordaeron. Here's how to get and complete all of them, including both Alliance and Horde quests, and the rewards they provide.

How Many Ruins of Lordareon Quests Are There?

There's a total of 10 quests exclusively for Ruins of Lordaeron, including both Horde and Alliance-aligned quests, though Horde ironically gets the lion's share of them. One of the quests, Crest of Lordaeron, is available to both factions with the same reward provided.

Note that this means you can only complete the quests tied to your character's faction, so if you're aligned with the Horde, you cannot complete the Alliance quests, and vice versa.

How to Complete All Alliance Ruins of Lordaeron Quests

There are four Ruins of Lordaeron quests available for the Alliance faction. Note that the Crest of Lordaeron quest is identical for both Alliance and Horde players, but is nonetheless listed for both factions below respectively.

NOTE: Remember that you and/or your party members can always use 'Share Quest' to ensure everyone is on the same page with all available quests! Just make sure that you've completed any necesssary pre-requisites for the quests and also meet the level requirement, otherwise you won't be able to accept them from the sharer! The only quest that reportedly CANNOT be shared, regardless of your status with other quests, is 'Remember That I Love You' (Alliance).

Pickup Location : Captain Truman inside Ruins of Lordaeron dungeon

Rewards : Grave Shroud, Slain Baron's Signet, Monstrous Cleaver

This is a pretty straightforward quest that's self-contained inside the dungeon itself. Speak to the undead NPC named Captain Truman on your way through the dungeon (he'll be standing at the end of an elevated path) to get the quest. He wants you to defeat the Baron and bring his head back to him as proof.

The Baron is one of the dungeon's bosses that wanders an open grassy area on the southeast side of the dungeon. His model resembles the city grunts you see in the Undercity and he wields melee weapons in each of his three hands. There are no notable mechanics to speak of in this encounter, so just have your designated tank keep him distracted while the DPS chip away his health.

Once felled, make sure to loot the body for his head (item is called 'Head of the Baron') and return to Captain Truman to turn in the quest for your rewards.

Pickup Location: Bloodied Insignia item inside Ruins of Lordaeron dungeon

Rewards: Duty Bound Leggings, Remembrance Armor

This quest is obtained from an Alliance insignia item that drops randomly from the dungeon's skeleton mobs. Use it from your inventory to start the quest. To complete it, you need to collect 10 Bloodied Insignias , which luckily drop from a variety of Elite mobs in the dungeon.

While you can grind regular Skeleton mobs from them, the best drop rates are from the Mangled Cadaver (9.34%), the Fallen Berserker (9.29%), the Fallen Necromancer (8.58%), and the Flesh Golem (7.61%). Other mobs such as Skeletal Mages, Skeletal Soldiers, Ghouls, Plague Ghouls, and Ragged Ghouls also drop the Bloodied Insignias, but their drop rate is nearly cut in half.

Either way, once you've collected 10 Bloodied Insignias, you then need to bring them to General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind City to complete the quest and get your rewards.

Pickup Location: Crest of Lordaeron item inside Ruins of Lordaeron dungeon

This quest is unlocked by obtaining the Crest of Lordaeron item during the dungeon from one of a few possible spawn points along the main path. Those spawn points include:

Directly to the right from the dungeon's main entrance, up a staircase to a tower.

On the southeast side of the dungeon, behind a door where a Banshee enemy can spawn from.

A hallway leading to a room adjacent to where the Bjork boss spawns. The crest can be at the foot of the stairs there.

On a wall on the northwest side of Bjork's spawn area.

Wherever it does spawn, interact with the large gold crest (often on the side of a tower) to get the item, and then use it from your inventory to start the quest.

You need to bring this crest to Lady Dena Kennedy in Stormwind City to complete the quest and get your reward.

Pickup Location: Blood-Stained Letter item inside Ruins of Lordaeron dungeon

IMPORTANT NOTE: As mentioned above, this quest CANNOT be shared!

To get this quest, you need to obtain the Blood-Stained Letter item from the Lordaeron Graveyard area inside the dungeon, conveniently close to where Rath'mael spawns.

Once you have it, bring the letter to Orphan Matron Nightingale in the Cathedral Square (56.3, 54.2) of Stormwind City. They'll mention someone named Jeremy Heartweaver who was brought to Stormwind after the attack on Lordaeron and then adopted to a woman in Duskwood.

Head to Duskwood as instructed to complete the quest and get your rewards.

How to Complete All Horde Ruins of Lordaeron Quests

There are six Ruins of Lordaeron quests available for the Horde faction. Note that the Crest of Lordaeron quest is identical for both Alliance and Horde players, but is nonetheless listed for both factions below respectively.

Pickup Location: Tabitha Heartweaver in Silverpine Forest at (44.5, 43.0)

Rewards: Tabitha's Cuffs, Edwards' Knife

To get this quest, speak to Tabitha Heartweaver in Silverpine Forest at (44.5, 43.0) in The Sepulcher area (a convenient flight path stop), and she'll ask you to investigate the disappearance of her husband Edward Heartweaver in the Lordaeron ruins.

As you progress the dungeon, Edward's corpse is located in the Lordaeron Graveyard area, near where the final boss Rath'mael spawns. Interact with it to fulfill the objective, and you'll then need to report back to Tabitha at The Sepulcher to complete the quest.

This quest functions much the same as the Alliance variant of it. While in the dungeon, you need to find and pick up the Crest of Lordaeron from one of several possible spawn locations, including:

You then need to bring this crest to Oran Snakewrithe in the Undercity to complete the quest and get your reward.

Pickup Location: Morbin Lightbane in the Undercity at (57.8, 89.8)

Rewards: Spare Part Bindings, The Stitcher

To start this quest, you first need to pick it up from Morbin Ligthbane in the Undercity at (57.8, 89.8) at the Apothecarium. He'll ask you to retrieve "replacements" to help rebuild the paladins of the Forsaken in the form of Intact Limbs.

To be precise, you need to collect 25 Intact Limbs , which you can get as a drop from most if not all of the dungeon's various mobs. The drop rate is also quite resonable across the board, so just focus your efforts on a steady stream of mobs until you've gathered enough for the objective.

Once you have enough, return to Morbin Lightbane in Undercity and turn them in to him to complete the quest and get your rewards.

Pickup Location: Theodore Griffs in the Undercity at (46.6, 72.0) in the Apothecarium

This particular quest is locked behind the following questchain that starts at The Sepulcher with Apothecary Renferrel (42.9, 40.9).

Once you've completed the entire A Recipe For Death questline, then The New Plague quest should become available for you to pick up from Theodore Griffs in the Apothecarium in the Undercity. Essentially, you can turn and grab it right in that same area after turning in the third leg of A Recipe For Death to Faranell.

For this quest, you need to collect a unique item called The Highly Toxic Strain from the Witherfang boss in the Ruins of Lordaeron dungeon. Once you have it, bring it back to Theodore Griffs to complete the quest and get your rewards.

Pickup Location: Deathguard Kristof in Tirisfal Glades at (65.2, 60.2)

Rewards: Forsaken Greataxe, Gnarled Necromancer's Staff

This particular quest is locked behind the following questchain that starts in Tirisfal Glades with Deathguard Linnea at (65.5, 60.2), a short distance northeast from Undercity near the town of Brill.

Once you've completed the required questchain, then The Wrath of Rath'mael should become available for you to pick up from Deathguard Kristof nearby in the town of Brill. They'll ask you to kill Rath'mael in the Ruins of Lordaeron, who is the final boss of the dungeon and thus the objective is unmissable.

Once Rath'mael is slain, return to Deathguard Kristof to complete the quest and get your rewards.

Pickup Location: Abominable Head that drops from The Baron enemy in the Ruins of Lordaeron dungeon

Rewards: Grave Shroud, Slain Baron's Signet, Monstrous Cleaver

This quest becomes available upon getting a dropped item from the Baron boss in the Ruins of Lordaeron dungeon called the Abominable Head. Use it from your inventory to start the Unending Torment quest, which is actually an entire questchain consisting of five parts.

Toxic Skullcap from Tawny Grisette in the Trade Quarter

Blisterweed from a pot near the Herbalism Trainer, and

Essence of Agony from the Poison Vendor in the Rogues' Quarter

Stand on the ledge overlooking the pool of green liquid in front of the machinery and use the quest item, then return to Faranell.

Make sure to complete all of these quests to get all the EXP and item rewards from Faranell.

articles.title: How to Get Fuses - Rob Run Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Fuses are an item that you can add to your base in Rob Run to help protect your property. The more you have, the more defenses you can give your house to make
articles.body:
Fuses are an item that you can add to your base in Rob Run to help protect your property. The more you have, the more defenses you can give your house to make sure that other players don't steal from you. They use Decoders to break into your place. Finding these fuses can be tricky, especially if you're trying to gather up equipment to protect yourself. In this guide, we're going to share with you how to get fuses while playing Rob Run.

The best way to get fuses is by buying them from the Black Market. You can find them for sale under the Construction Tab, in the Basic Goods section. You can buy the most basic ones when you have a level 1 Settlement house and have at least $10,000. This unlocks the basic fuses, and then you need to spend $20,000 to buy them.

The basic fuses add a point to your home's defenses. Homes have a base starting defense level. For example, your level 1 Settlement house has five points in defenses, meaning another player needs at least five Decoders to break into it. When you add a basic fuse to your home security network, it goes up to six points, and another player needs six Decoders, or two Epic Decoders, to break into it.

If you want to more defenses from fuses, use the epic rarity fuse, which increases your defense by three points, or the legendary fuse increasing your defenses by five points. The epic fuse requires you to have a level 2 Settlement house and $150,000 to unlock it, while the legendary fuse requires you to have a level 3 Settlement house and $500,000 to unlock it.

Alternatively, you can get legendary fuses from the Suspicious Door at Lenny's Motel. You can exchange one epic fuse and $250,000 for a legendary fuse.

When you have any of the three fuses, approach the Security System of your house, fence, or any of the additional pieces of property you've added to your home, such as the Grow House. Each of these has a different Security System that you can interact with, and other players need to bypass them to access your stuff.

When you interact with it, you'll open up a window where you can place new fuses on the left side, increasing your home's defenses. You can see the number at the top, next to the house icon. Below those are alarm systems, which give you a notification (and others who are in your clan) that someone is trying to break into your property. You only get this notification if you're online, though.

articles.title: UK’s National Health Service Is Urging Gamers to Protect Their Hands Ahead of GTA 6 Launch
articles.summary: The UK’s National Health Service is giving players advice to help them avoid straining their hands once GTA 6 finally releases on November 19.
articles.body:
The UK’s National Health Service is giving players advice to help them avoid straining their hands once GTA 6 finally releases on November 19.

The service’s humorous PSA was posted to Instagram on November 16, just three days before Rockstar’s highly anticipated game launches. The post includes several photos taken by the NHS’s social media manager, whose hand has been wrapped up tight in a cast.

The poor employee explained that they underwent surgery to “remove a lump” from their hand, which they said is particularly “bad timing” due to GTA 6’s imminent release. To help others avoid injuring themselves and being unable to play, they shared some tips to keep your ligaments in tip-top shape.

For starters, the NHS is urging players to “try and take regular breaks.” This helps avoid eye strain, and getting up from your gaming chair or sofa every couple of hours is good for circulation, relieving muscle stiffness, and providing mental clarity. (That’s right — you might actually play better if you take regular breaks.)

The NHS’s post was particularly concerned with RSI, or repetitive strain injury, which it described as “pain that can be caused by repeated movement of part of the body, such as hands and fingers.”

RSI can happen for a number of reasons; sports like tennis or golfing can be culprits, as can jobs like hairdressing (using scissors and other tools), working an assembly line, and even typing at your computer.

While RSI is a general umbrella term for these types of injuries, carpal tunnel is a more specific condition that falls under the RSI label. Gamers are prone to this type of strain, due to pressing buttons quickly and repetitively, moving a joystick back and forth, and gripping one’s controller or mouse tightly while playing.

While a repetitive strain injury might legitimately be something you could call out of work for, you might have a hard time getting the time off, given how many players are already planning on taking time off from their jobs to roam around Vice City. There's already been a 17% increase in time-off requests from employees for November 19, and even world governments like Germany and Australia are talking about the game’s upcoming impact on the workforce.

In fact, estimates show that GTA 6 is likely to drain $1 billion from the US economy, since so many people will be staying at home to play on November 19. Some companies are getting a jump on the amount of ‘sick’ employees they’ll likely have by offering the time off ahead of time, with tech giant Logitech giving staff the option to take personal days for major video game releases. Just remember to take regular breaks — Vice City will be just fine without you for a few moments.

Subway is getting on the GTA 6 hype train with a sandwich themed after the highly anticipated game.

The sandwich chain announced today that it is giving its Miami-exclusive Cubano Pulled Pork Melt a GTA 6 "reskin" in time for the new game. The sandwich is being renamed the Vice City Cubano and, as noted, is only available in the city of Miami. The sandwich comes either as a six-inch or footlong sub and features hardwood-smoked pulled pork, black forest ham, melted provolone, pickles, and mustard on freshly baked artisan Italian bread.

Subway confirmed that the sandwich will be available both in-store and for delivery for those who don't plan to leave their couch when GTA 6 is released. You can see an image of it below.

Subway isn't the only fast food place getting in on on the GTA 6 hype. Popeyes is also releasing a Vice City-themed chicken sandwich that it calls "Spice City." It will be available for one week starting November 19 and is available at participating locations for in-store pick up or delivery. Finally, there are also a bunch of Miami-based dining options and stores that have officially teamed up with Rockstar to provide themed meals and drinks based on GTA. The most notable of the bunch is a partnership with Skinny Louie, a burger chain based out of Florida.

The chain has been turned into Burger Shot , a fast food joint prominently featured in the GTA franchise. The menu, uniforms, packaging, and signange for Skinny Louie has been completely refitted with Burger Shot branding, which will remain in place until the end of the year. Rockstar's marketing power has reached unprecedented levels, even prompting other places that don't have a partnership in place to try and ride the hype waves.

articles.title: Hacker behind 2022 GTA VI leaks pleads guilty
articles.summary: Arion Kurtaj, a member of the Lapsus$ cybercrime group who leaked 90 videos of Grand Theft Auto VI in 2022 and hacked other big companies, pleaded guilty on Monday.
articles.body: Arion Kurtaj, a member of the Lapsus$ cybercrime group who leaked 90 videos of Grand Theft Auto VI in 2022 and hacked other big companies, pleaded guilty on Monday, according to the UK’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS). Kurtaj, who is now 21, hacked BT/EE sometime between August and November 2021, and starting in early November of that year, the company “noted a marked increase in unauthorised SIM swaps of their customers mobile phones.” He was charged for those offenses and moved to a hotel for his “own protection” in September 2022, but “breached his bail conditions to carry out further hacks on major companies using a mobile phone, the hotel TV’s Wi-Fi and a firestick,” including hacks on Rockstar Games, Uber, and Revolut, the CPS says. He was sentenced to life in a secure hospital in December 2023 because of his autism, but in January, Kurtaj was deemed fit for trial and moved to prison, the BBC reports. Kurtaj is set to be sentenced on November 23rd. GTA VI will be released on November 19th.

articles.title: Former James Bond Actor George Lazenby Gives Robert Pattinson Advice After Batman Star Scores Iconic Role
articles.summary: George Lazenby, who formerly portrayed James Bond, is giving Robert Pattinson some sage advice after the Batman actor scored the historic and highly coveted role.
articles.body:
George Lazenby, who formerly portrayed James Bond, is giving Robert Pattinson some sage advice after the Batman actor scored the historic and highly coveted role.

After a lengthy and secretive casting process stacked with some of Britain’s greatest actors, Robert Pattinson was officially revealed as the next James Bond on November 16, 2026. This marks the latest in a string of high-profile parts Pattinson has played lately, which include Batman , Chris Hansen in Primetime , Antinous in Nolan’s Odyssey, and Scytale in Dune: Part Three.

It’s safe to say that Pattinson is no stranger to being the face of a franchise, what with his experience playing Edward Cullen in the Twilight saga and Batman in Matt Reeves’ take on the caped crusader. But James Bond is a different beast entirely, as fans’ reactions to this latest news have already proven this fact.

Luckily, he’s not alone. A slew of other actors have taken up the 007 mantle before him, including Lazenby, who portrayed the character in 1969's On Her Majesty’s Secret Service . Lazenby took the opportunity to give Pattinson some useful tips before he steps into M16.

“I hear they've announced the new James Bond,” Lazenby wrote in a post shared on social media. “Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world. But remember to enjoy yourself. Let's see if you'll have [a] ‘This never happened to the other fella!’ moment. All the best, mate, George xx.”

It’s safe to say Pattinson is already having one of those moments, given the energetic opinions we’ve seen on social media already. Many fans are ecstatic about him being cast as Bond, given his extensive filmography playing the tortured hero; others, however, aren’t so sure that he’s a good fit, while others are joking that he’s being too “greedy” by taking up all the best roles in Hollywood.

I hear they've announced the new James Bond @007... Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world. But remember to enjoy yourself. Let's see if you'll have "this never happened to the other fella" moment. All the best mate, George xx — George Lazenby (@lazenbyofficial) November 16, 2026

I hear they've announced the new James Bond @007... Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world. But remember to enjoy yourself. Let's see if you'll have "this never happened to the other fella" moment. All the best mate, George xx

It’s certainly been quite a year for Pattinson, who’s had a nice few films that have dominated the box office this year. He, along with Tom Holland and Zendaya, is one of the most recognizable faces in the business right now — and it proves how far he’s come from his days as Edward Cullen.

In fact, Pattinson was apparently so coveted for Bond that he was reportedly offered a more lucrative contract for fewer films than other actors in the running, which included Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor, and Nicholas Hoult.

For now, we’ll just have to wait and see what Pattinson’s Bond has to offer. In the meantime, you can look forward to watching him in Dune: Part Three this December.
